effective.basis: TCG release of LCYW-EN102 (Legendary Collection 3: Yugi's World Mega Pack), the first printing carrying the Damage Step exclusion

transitions.historical_text: Activate only by paying 1000 Life Points when a monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard, Special Summon 1 Level 4 monster from your Deck.
transitions.modern_text: When a monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard (except during the Damage Step): Pay 1000 Life Points; Special Summon 1 Level 4 monster from your Deck.
transitions.summary: Activation window narrowed: v1 (LCYW-EN102) added '(except during the Damage Step)', which the v0 text (LODT-ENSE2) does not carry. v0 triggers whenever a monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard, and battle destruction happens inside the Damage Step, so under the era text the trap had to be usable there for its battle-destruction case to function at all. The same printing moved the 1000 Life Point payment from 'Activate only by paying 1000 Life Points when ...' into PSCT cost position, which does not change that it is a cost.

effective.basis: TCG release of the first printing carrying the current text (YGLD-ENB39, Yugi's Legendary Decks)

transitions.historical_text: When a monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard (except during the Damage Step): Pay 1000 Life Points; Special Summon 1 Level 4 monster from your Deck.
transitions.modern_text: When a monster you control is destroyed by a card effect and sent to the Graveyard (except during the Damage Step): Pay 1000 LP; Special Summon 1 Level 4 monster from your Deck.
transitions.summary: Functional erratum: 'When a monster you control is destroyed and sent to the Graveyard' becomes 'When a monster you control is destroyed by a card effect and sent to the Graveyard', so the modern card no longer triggers on battle destruction at all. The modern script encodes the restriction in its cfilter, which requires both c:IsReason(REASON_EFFECT) and c:IsReason(REASON_DESTROY) on an EVENT_TO_GRAVE trigger.

coverage.gap_reason: Project Ignis ships no historical implementation of this card; reproducing the era behaviour needs a custom script and a reserved passcode

gap.behavioural_impact: In a period format Soul Rope cannot be used when your monster is destroyed in battle - the era text's main case - because the modern card only triggers on destruction by a card effect and is barred from the Damage Step.

review.notes: upstream_implementations lists only 511001593 'Soul Rope (Anime)', a distinct card whose text ('When a monster(s) you control is destroyed: Pay 1000 LP; ...') matches no lineage version (ratio 0.7388) and which drops the 'sent to the Graveyard' requirement entirely; it is not substitutable, so the gap stands. It is a useful reference for the shape an era script needs: EVENT_DESTROYED with EFFECT_FLAG_DAMAGE_STEP and a cfilter carrying no REASON_EFFECT/REASON_DESTROY test, plus the 'sent to the Graveyard' requirement the anime card lacks. Dating: v0's earliest tcg date is tcg-oce 2008-01-01 at YEAR precision, with the NA/EU Special Edition at 2008-06-18; either way v0 is the text in force at both the GOAT and Edison snapshots, since v1 is 2012-09-29. No supported period snapshot falls inside the intermediate window 2012-09-29 .. 2015-11-12, so I attached no resulting_implementation to the first change - the intermediate version is not needed by any format. CAVEAT on that first change: the packet establishes that the '(except during the Damage Step)' exclusion was added, not that era policy independently permitted Damage Step activation of a trap whose trigger is general destruction rather than battle destruction specifically. I recorded the text fact and the inference, and flagged nothing further, because the era version is v0 under either reading and the gap is required by the second change regardless.
